reason: The text depicts Pharaoh (the elite ruler) repeatedly making poor decisions despite overwhelming evidence, while his servants (regular people) demonstrate superior judgment. Notably, when the plagues intensify, Pharaoh's servants confront him: 'How long will this be a snare to us? Send the men away, that they may serve the Lord their God. Don't you know yet that Egypt is destroyed?' (Exodus 9:28). The servants recognize the catastrophic consequences that Pharaoh refuses to acknowledge. Similarly, Egypt's magicians (elite experts) eventually admit 'This is the finger of God' and fail to replicate later plagues. Meanwhile, regular Egyptians who heeded God's word and took precautions were protected. The narrative shows that those with direct access to information and power (Pharaoh, the magicians) persist in destructive denial, while ordinary people demonstrate clearer perception of reality and better practical wisdom.
